what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tool in tools/documents-as-list-rows: a folder of markdown documents the person granted, shown as the rows of a list (each document's frontmatter its fields, read a page at a time), a field changed by rewriting that document's frontmatter while it is the document read, and long documents split into one document per item. They run on the person's own computer, over the folder they granted.

payload.label: Show a folder of my documents as the rows of a list
payload.job: Read the markdown documents in a folder I granted as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time
payload.description: Reads every .md, .markdown and .txt document under the granted folder (or `folder` inside it), skipping folders whose names start with a dot and links that point outside it, in name order, and answers one page of rows: { id (its path under the folder), title, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its bytes), values } where values holds its frontmatter as note.<key> and its file facts as file.<key>. A page holds up to `limit` rows (200 by default, 2,000 at most) and answers `next` while more remain; pass it as `after` for the next page, so any number of documents is read. `match` keeps the documents whose path fits a glob such as */SKILL.md. `backlinks` adds file.backlinks, worked out over the whole folder. Nothing is copied: the documents are the rows. Optional content:true adds exact complete UTF-8 text including frontmatter in bounded linked pieces, keeping the original parent ID and metadata. Child pieces name their parent, part number and total; pass the opaque next cursor unchanged. No body is silently truncated.

folder.description: A folder inside the granted folder, written /a/b; the granted folder itself when left out.

match.description: A glob the document's path under `folder` must fit, as */SKILL.md.

after.description: The `next` of the page before; left out for the first page.

limit.description: Rows a page holds (200 when left out).

backlinks.description: Work out which documents link to each row (reads the whole folder).

most_bytes.description: The most bytes the answer may take: the page ends at the last row that fits (a door answers a run within one bounded message).

content.description: Opt in to complete document text: original parent row ID plus stable linked child rows for bounded pieces. Join all consecutively numbered pieces; a cursor pins an unfinished document identity. An object overrides the generic content field names and nominal part_bytes.

sections.description: An existing splitDocuments heading/row mapping, consumed as DATA. Emits stable virtual section rows and original raw remainder spans; original parent keeps metadata and all source bytes are preserved without a duplicate full-body row.

omit_fields.description: Explicitly omit only declared regenerable derived file caches. Defaults to none. Source/frontmatter fields, file identity/path and content text may never be omitted.

exclude.description: Exclude document paths relative to folder by glob, using the same semantics as match.

paths.description: Read only these exact absolute-within-root document names, without recursively walking other folders. Every path still obeys the granted root and symlink checks.

text_extensions.description: Explicit text-file extensions allowed for paths, such as py or mjs. Does not expand the ordinary document-folder scan. Content must be valid UTF-8 and is never executed.

paths_file.description: Name of a JSON array positive catalogue under the granted root, instead of embedding paths in a bounded list record. Read through the same files owner, identity checked and refused if it exceeds the existing per-document byte bound.

provenance.source: Written for the Workshop: a folder of documents queried as rows by their frontmatter, in the way a notes vault's database view reads its notes

payload.description: The same rows as tool:read-documents-as-list-rows, read from the person's Namespace files through the run's records door (list_files and read_file, every file read by its name) instead of a folder on their computer. payload.label: Change fields of documents in my folder list
payload.job: Change or remove fields of documents' frontmatter in a folder I granted, each only if the document is still the one I read
payload.description: For each row { id, values: { note.<key>: value or null }, if_identity } rewrites only the frontmatter lines of the keys named: a value sets the key, null removes it, and other keys, comments and the body stay byte for byte. A value must fit the kind the folder's property-types.json gives the property; file facts cannot be written. When if_identity is given and the document changed since it was read, the change is refused and nothing is merged. The new bytes replace the document in one rename, and the answer is each changed document's new values and identity.

folder.description: A folder inside the granted folder the ids are under; the granted folder itself when left out.

id.description: The document's id from its row, as /notes/plan.md.

values.description: note.<key> to its new value, or null to remove the key.

if_identity.description: The identity from the row that was read (1f:...).

provenance.source: Written for the Workshop: a conditional write keyed by the content identity that was read, so a change made meanwhile is never lost

payload.label: Split a long document of many items into one document per item
payload.job: Turn long markdown documents that hold many numbered items (rules, lessons, questions) into one document per item with its fields in frontmatter, so each item is a row of a folder list
payload.description: Reads the documents a mapping names and finds the items by the mapping's heading and table-row patterns, merging pieces of one item from several documents. Each item becomes `<id>.md`: frontmatter (id, then the fields the mapping captures, groups and flags) and its parts under headings. Text that belongs to no item is kept in one leftover file per document. Every line read is placed (the report counts both), and pieces with the same words are written once. It refuses a folder that is not empty. It knows no item kind: everything comes from the mapping.

mapping.description: The mapping file, relative to root (the README describes its keys).

root.description: The folder the mapping's documents are relative to.

out.description: An empty folder under root for the item documents.

leftover.description: A folder under root for each document's text that belongs to no item.

output_schema.description: { items, lines_in, lines_placed, leftover_lines, identical_pieces_merged } as JSON; exit 2 with a reason when the mapping or a document could not be read, the lines did not add up or the folder is not empty.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the mapping with them from a few of their items, run it with --check in place of --out and --leftover first and read the report with them: how many items, how many lines are leftover and why. Then run it into an empty folder and open two or three of the item documents with them before anything else changes.

provenance.source: Written for the Workshop: a fence-aware markdown sectioner driven by a declarative mapping
